extra_change: Narrowed the pass-1 trigger to holders with OC in range now (_unit_oc_at_position(...) > 0). Reason: test_ai_objective_assignment_fixes went from 1 known failure (V9R: 6/1) to 2 failures (5/2) with root as written. Its 'one of two stays' case has two units on an objective. Their snapshots carry no status (=UNDEPLOYED), so their in-range OC is 0 and friendly_oc does not count them. Root's premise ('the holder is already in friendly_oc') was false there, both phantom holders were pinned, and neither added OC. A battle-shocked holder behaves the same way in real games. After the narrowing the suite is back to 6/1 (only the known base failure). The cost: root's phantom-holder effect (s7408 r3 Tankbustas, friendly 0 vs enemy 0) no longer fires. Test test_holder_without_oc_in_range_keeps_base_ledger pins this.

risks: (1) Evidence of value is thin: one finding flips (s7454 r3), and with a different unit and mode than measured. The confirmed s7455 r2 finding (+5.92) is not reached. (2) Co-holders on objectives we do not control are now pinned (both hold with oc_consumed 0, where the base freed one); this is unmeasured. (3) The pass-2.5 path is covered only by the unit test; it never fired in the replays. (4) The narrowing to holders with OC in range drops root's phantom/battle-shocked effect (s7408); that change is mine, not the judge's. (5) Full-game and secondary-VP effects are unknown, so the bench must decide. Param 0 restores V9R exactly: verified on one Custodes-mirror seed.
